entry.title: Updates for Chrome 157 beta
entry.content:
The https://collector.openwebdocs.org/ project (v10.20.16) found new features shipping in Chromium 157 beta which was released today. Currently, the collector covers about 90% of BCD, so the following list might not be exhaustive. Also, if a feature is in Canary/behind flags, it is not considered here. If a feature is missing, one reason can be that the IDL is not yet in a specification or in webref.

Chrome 157 stable releases on November 3, 2026. This PR needs to be merged before/with the BCD release on October 29, 2026.

With this PR, BCD will consider the following features as shipping in Chromium 157:

HTML setters, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5054329641893888. @tunetheweb can you review this part?

  • api.CharacterData.afterHTML
  • api.CharacterData.afterHTMLUnsafe
  • api.CharacterData.beforeHTML
  • api.CharacterData.beforeHTMLUnsafe
  • api.CharacterData.replaceWithHTML
  • api.CharacterData.replaceWithHTMLUnsafe
  • api.Element.setHTMLUnsafe.options_runscripts_parameter
  • api.Element.afterHTML
  • api.Element.afterHTMLUnsafe
  • api.Element.appendHTML
  • api.Element.appendHTMLUnsafe
  • api.Element.beforeHTML
  • api.Element.beforeHTMLUnsafe
  • api.Element.prependHTML
  • api.Element.prependHTMLUnsafe
  • api.Element.replaceWithHTML
  • api.Element.replaceWithHTMLUnsafe
  • api.ShadowRoot.setHTMLUnsafe.options_runscripts_parameter
  • api.ShadowRoot.appendHTML
  • api.ShadowRoot.appendHTMLUnsafe
  • api.ShadowRoot.prependHTML
  • api.ShadowRoot.prependHTMLUnsafe
  • api.TrustedHTMLParserOptions (I removed two non-shipping keys here [runScripts and sanitizer], they don't appear in the IDL, cc @tunetheweb)
  • api.TrustedTypePolicy.createParserOptions (new key)

WebTransport reliability attributes, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5094058497277952 (Chromestatus says 158)

  • api.WebTransport.reliability
  • api.WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly_static

WebTransport responseHeaders, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5194104408506368 (Chromestatus says 156)

  • api.WebTransport.responseHeaders

CSS anchor-valid and anchor-visible, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5136123851571200

  • css.properties.position-visibility.anchor-valid
  • css.properties.position-visibility.anchor-visible

CSS text-decoration-inset, https://chromestatus.com/feature/5178263526834176

  • css.properties.text-decoration-inset
  • css.properties.text-decoration-inset.auto

See also https://chromestatus.com/release-notes/157

Some notes:

  • The spec for https://chromestatus.com/feature/5171478175809536 was only merged yesterday, I will have to re-run Collection next week when I have the IDL.
  • The spec for https://chromestatus.com/feature/5172548013916160 is not available yet. I could try to get the IDL manually.
  • https://chromestatus.com/feature/5087964794322944 will need a run on Android.

entry.title: `api.Window.unload_event`: set as partially implemented in Chrome 155
entry.content:
Summary

Chrome no longer fires unload by default, so we ought to mark it as partially implemented.

Test results and supporting details

Chrome has made unload fully opt in. Note that this is an implementer deprecation, not one we can apply the feature in general (WHATWG never took up discouragement by specification, see whatwg/html#6026).

entry.title: Add WebAssembly reference instructions (ref.*)
entry.content:
Adds webassembly.instructions.ref_null, ref_is_null, ref_func, ref_as_non_null, ref_eq, ref_test and ref_cast.

Summary

Adds compat data for the seven WebAssembly reference instructions (spec "Reference Instructions" section):

  • webassembly.instructions.ref_null
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_is_null
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_func
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_as_non_null
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_eq
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_test
  • webassembly.instructions.ref_cast

Structure follows table_init.json, per @chrisdavidmills’s guidance on the issue.

Test results and supporting details

Versions match the proposal-level features each instruction shipped with, as already recorded in BCD and web-features:

  • ref.null, ref.is_null, ref.func: reference types (webassembly.reference-types): Chrome 96, Firefox 79, Safari 15.1
  • ref.as_non_null: typed function references (webassembly.typedFunctionReferences): Chrome 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18
  • ref.eq, ref.test, ref.cast: garbage collection (webassembly.garbage-collection): Chrome 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2Safari 18
  • ref.eq, ref.test, ref.cast: garbage collection (webassembly.garbage-collection): Chrome 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2

Also cross-checked against https://webassembly.org/features/.

spec_url anchors follow the convention used by table_init and validate against @webref/xref. Tags use the existing wasm-reference-types, wasm-typed-fun-refs and wasm-garbage-collection web-features IDs.

mdn_url is intentionally omitted: the MDN pages are in a companion mdn/content PR, and the URLs can be added once they're live.

npm test: format and lint pass; unit tests 341/341.

Related issues

Relates to mdn/content#37854

entry.title: feat: add COEP and COOP Report-Only header compatibility data
entry.content:

  • Add compatibility data for the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy-Report-Only header.

entry.title: fix(update-browser-releases): link Chrome 155+ release notes to Chrome Status
entry.content:
Summary

Makes the Chrome release updater link Chrome Status release notes for Chrome 155 and later, and adds the missing Chrome Status links for Chrome 155 to 158 in chrome.json, chrome_android.json, and webview_android.json.

Test results and supporting details

  • Selects the release-notes source by version: Chrome Status from 155, developer.chrome.com release notes for 124 to 154, and new-in-chrome posts for 54 to 123.
  • Chrome 155's developer.chrome.com page returns 404, so the previous lookup recorded no link. chromestatus.com/release-notes/155 returns 200.
  • Records Chrome Status links for beta, nightly, and planned releases too, since Chrome Status publishes them ahead of stable (156 to 158 return 200).
  • Covers the version boundaries with unit tests.

Related issues

Fixes #30877.

entry.title: fix(html): add notes for dialog closedby=any touch propagation bug
entry.content:
Fixes #30474

<dialog closedby="any"> has a touch event propagation bug in Chrome 134–153
and Firefox 141+: tapping the backdrop closes the dialog but does not cancel
the event, causing click listeners on elements behind the backdrop to fire.

Changes:

  • Chrome: converted to array — clean entry for 154+ (fixed via
    bug 425579196), plus a 134–153 entry with a note
  • Firefox: added notes to the 141+ entry linking to
    bug 2022750 (still unfixed as of Firefox 156)
  • chrome_android, edge, and firefox_android correctly mirror their
    desktop entries — no additional changes needed

entry.title: html/elements/iframe: add local-network, local-network-access, and loopback-network allow directives
entry.content:
Fixes #30831

Adds three missing Permission Policy directive entries to html.elements.iframe.allow:

  • local-network: Chrome 145, Firefox 153, experimental: false
  • loopback-network: Chrome 145, Firefox 153, experimental: false
  • local-network-access: Chrome 142, Firefox false, experimental: true (legacy alias, superseded by the two above)

Firefox support verified via Bugzilla bug 1978550 (RESOLVED FIXED); network.lna.blocking defaults to true from the Firefox 153 release tag.

Note: http.headers.Permissions-Policy entries for these directives correctly remain false — Firefox has not implemented HTTP header parsing for Permissions-Policy (bug 1531012 is still open).

entry.title: Add pathLength to SVG geometry elements
entry.content:
Summary

  • Adds pathLength to <path>, <circle>, <ellipse>, <line>, <polygon>, <polyline> and <rect>
  • Support versions reflect actual rendering, meaning stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset scaled by pathLength
  • <path>: Chrome 50, Firefox 6, Safari 14
  • Other shapes: Chrome 57, Firefox 61, Safari 14
  • Safari reflected the attribute in the DOM long before it affected rendering

Test results and supporting details

  • Tested in Chrome 154, Firefox 157 and Safari 27 by drawing each shape to a canvas with stroke-dasharray in pathLength units and sampling pixels along the stroke
  • Chrome 50, <path>: https://crbug.com/536217 (r373110)
  • Chrome 57, other shapes: https://crbug.com/596043, https://codereview.chromium.org/2525233002 (r435194)
  • Firefox 6, <path>: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=643419
  • Firefox 61, other shapes: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1325320 (the stroke-dash code checks for <path> at FIREFOX_60_0_RELEASE and any shape at FIREFOX_61_0_RELEASE)
  • Safari 14: https://webkit.org/b/72401 (r254657, January 2020, WebKit 610), scaling applied to any SVGGeometryElement

Related issues

  • mdn/mdn#852

entry.title: Add Notifications API `navigate` option
entry.content:

Firefox 158 adds support for Notification.navigator — the ability to specify a URL to navigate to once a notification is clicked.

#30755 adds api.Notification.navigate (the property), but there are two more data points required:

  • api.Notification.Notification.navigate (the constructor option)
  • api.ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification.options_navigate_parameter (the service worker showNotification() option)

This PR adds both.

entry.title: Add svgView() fragment identifier to SVG <view>
entry.content:
Summary

  • Adds the svgView() fragment identifier, as in image.svg#svgView(viewBox(0,0,50,50)), with its viewBox(), preserveAspectRatio() and transform() parameters
  • Marks transform() as partial in Firefox: it’s applied around the center of the viewport, and after the view box in viewport pixels instead of user units
  • Versions follow the parent <view> element and its other subfeatures (I think it’s safe to assume they were implemented at the same time)

Test results and supporting details

  • Tested in Chrome 154, Firefox 157 and Safari 27 by drawing <img src="test.svg#svgView(…)"> to a canvas and measuring where known shapes land
  • viewBox(), preserveAspectRatio() and translate() in transform() give the same result in all three
  • transform(scale(0.5)) moves a square at 40,40 to 20,20 in Chrome and Safari, and to 45,45 in Firefox
  • WPT: svgview-transform.html and svgview-viewbox-then-transform.html fail only in Firefox
  • Firefox transform() bug: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2066140
  • Firefox 15 implemented <view> and svgView() together: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=512525
  • Safari ignores the fragment when drawing an image to a canvas that was never inserted into the page, which is a canvas bug rather than an svgView() one: https://webkit.org/b/322167

Related issues

  • mdn/mdn#852
